sections.overview: This Colombian freshwater catfish is endemic to the Magdalena–Cauca drainage. It is closely related to Pseudoplatystoma corruscans, whose range instead includes the São Francisco and Paraná basins.
sections.identification: It has broad, straight dark bars on its sides; P. corruscans is distinguished by a spotted pattern.
sections.habitat: It inhabits large river channels and floodplain lakes in the Magdalena basin.
sections.diet: Juveniles feed on other fishes, according to the cited basin assessment.
sections.behavior: It makes medium-distance longitudinal migrations within the river basin.
sections.reproduction: It reproduces throughout the year, with seasonal peaks during high water.
sections.ecology: Published color-pattern analyses distinguish its dark bars from the characteristic spots of P. corruscans. The taxonomic revision also recognizes P. metaense, an Orinoco congener.
sections.conservation: The 2014 global IUCN assessment listed it as Endangered. Colombia's 2024 national threatened-species resolution lists it as Critically Endangered.
